captions.instagram:
How does the brain work?

86 billion neurons, 100 trillion connections and about 20 watts. Take a 3D brain apart, fire a neuron, light up the areas you use to speak, and watch memories move while you sleep.

→ Your brain: about 1.4 kg of soft tissue, folded so a pillowcase-sized sheet fits in your skull.
→ Four lobes on each side, a cerebellum for balance, and a brainstem that keeps you breathing.
→ A neuron rests at −70 mV. Push it past −55 mV and it fires an all-or-nothing spike.
→ A stronger push means more spikes, not bigger ones, racing down a myelin-wrapped axon.
→ At a synapse, the spike releases chemicals that cross a gap 20 millionths of a millimetre wide.

Play with it yourself. It's free and open source: glassbox.how/brainclear (link in bio)

youtubeLong.title: How does the brain work? (interactive explainer)
youtubeLong.description:
86 billion neurons, 100 trillion connections and about 20 watts. Take a 3D brain apart, fire a neuron, light up the areas you use to speak, and watch memories move while you sleep.

▶ Play with the interactive version: https://glassbox.how/e/brainclear/
⌘ Source code (MIT): https://github.com/bdeeps/brainclear

In this video:
• Two halves, four lobes, one busy core. The cerebrum's two hemispheres each have frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes, wrapped in a folded cortex only 2 to 4 mm thick.
• Neurons fire all-or-nothing spikes. A neuron rests at about −70 mV.
• Synapses turn sparks into chemicals. At a synapse, the spike lets calcium in, vesicles spill neurotransmitter across a 20 nm gap, and receptors on the next cell open.
• Areas have jobs, but you use all of it. Vision is at the back, hearing on the temporal lobe, movement and touch on strips either side of the central sulcus, with huge areas for hands and lips.
• Memories are sorted by day and filed by night. The hippocampus tags new experiences, as the patient H.M.
• A hungry organ that needs its blood. At about 2% of body weight, the brain uses about 20% of the body's energy, about 20 W.
